content_html:
Episodic ↔ Semantic Metaphor

Wetland Pools → River System

Episodic memories are like wetland pools; semantic memory is like a river system. Overlap zones carry water from one to the other.

This metaphor translates the episodic–semantic continuum into an ecological landscape: episodic memories as local pools, semantic knowledge as the river system, with shared waters connecting them.

Episodic pools are local, time-bound, and fragile — each event is its own body of water, affected by weather and season. Semantic rivers integrate these flows, creating durable channels that shape the landscape of knowledge. The overlap zone represents the exchange: episodes sediment into semantic categories, and schemas guide how new episodes are stored and recalled.

This metaphor sits alongside the neuroscientific continuum (hippocampus ↔ cortex).

Pools = hippocampal binding of specific contexts;
River = cortical networks encoding decontextualized knowledge;
Estuary = consolidation and reconsolidation processes.
